posts.big_note: Forecast U.S. holiday spending for Nov–Dec 2026 — a record, up 4.2% over last year
posts.headline: Black Friday is here — and America is headed for a record $1.013 TRILLION holiday season. But a record total isn't more gifts: it's mostly higher prices.
posts.source: Source: NRF 2026 holiday forecast; Retail Council of Canada × Leger survey
posts.caption:
Black Friday is here — and America is headed for its first back-to-back trillion-dollar holiday.

The National Retail Federation forecasts $1.013 trillion in November–December spending, up 4.2% from last year's $972 billion. But a record total isn't a shopping boom — prices are up about 3%, so much of it is just paying more for the same cart. 56% of shoppers say the economy will shape what they buy.

North of the border it's the opposite: Canadians plan to spend about $64 less this year, around $911 each, as inflation and trade tensions weigh on budgets.

My take: a record built on higher prices isn't a boom — it's a bigger bill. Watch what you actually bring home, not the receipt total.

Are you spending more this year, or just paying more for the same? 👇

Source: National Retail Federation 2026 holiday forecast; Retail Council of Canada × Leger survey
Educational only — not financial advice.

But a record total isn't more gifts. With prices up around 3%, much of the 'record' is just paying more for the same cart — and 56% of shoppers say the economy will shape what they buy.
In Canada it's the reverse: shoppers plan to spend about $64 less this year, roughly $911 each, as inflation and U.S. trade tensions weigh on budgets.
